00315.title: Docetaxel 75 / cisplatin 75 / fluorouracil 1,000 · induction TPF
00315.setting: Induction treatment of stage III/IV non-metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, with a separately agreed definitive chemoradiation and/or surgery plan.
00315.purpose: Shrink and control the cancer before the next definitive local treatment. The team must record the subsequent chemoradiation and/or surgery plan; induction is not the complete treatment pathway.
00315.schedule: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² on Day 1, with fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day on Days 1–4. Repeat every 21 days for 3 cycles, unless progression or unacceptable toxicity changes the plan. After cycle 3, the multidisciplinary team confirms response, recovery and the definitive chemoradiation and/or surgery plan. No automatic radiotherapy date or universal subsequent regimen is authorised by selecting this induction route.
material_risks: Serious infection, febrile neutropenia, sepsis or bleeding from low blood counts
Kidney injury, electrolyte disturbance, hearing damage/tinnitus and peripheral neuropathy, which can persist
Nausea/vomiting, diarrhoea, mouth inflammation, dehydration and nutritional or swallowing difficulty
Fluorouracil cardiac toxicity and unexpectedly early/severe toxicity, including with DPD deficiency; hand-foot syndrome
Docetaxel hypersensitivity, fluid retention, fatigue, hair/nail/skin changes and reproductive or fertility effects
00315.discussion: Discuss the intended benefit and evidence limitations, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or persistent harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Confirm the exact indication and current licensed/off-label position.
limitations: TAX 324 used cisplatin 100 mg/m², so its numerical survival results must not be presented as the measured effect of 00315.
No benefit percentage is assigned to the current dose variant. Response after induction is not proof of cure.

TAX 323/324 compare TPF with PF induction. They do not establish a universal survival advantage for adding induction before chemoradiation. PARADIGM closed early with 145 patients; its three-year overall survival was 73% versus 78% (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.59–2.03; P=0.77), so lack of a statistically significant difference is not proof of equivalence.
support: Docetaxel premedication is dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for 3 days starting the day before docetaxel; at least 3 doses should precede treatment unless contraindicated. If oral premedication was missed, the source permits dexamethasone 20 mg IV at consultant discretion. This is not automatic permission to proceed. Reconcile the total steroid with antiemetic dexamethasone; do not add both schedules blindly.

Prescribe cisplatin pre- and post-hydration and electrolytes using current renal/cardiac status and local policy. The national source suggests saline/magnesium with optional potassium, but a reference list is not an individual fluid prescription. Monitor intake, urine output, renal function and electrolytes.

Document DPD phenotype and/or genotype before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously tested. Complete deficiency precludes fluorouracil; partial deficiency needs an individual starting-dose plan. Renal impairment can elevate uracil and misclassify phenotype; consider genotype. A normal result does not exclude all severe toxicity.
G-CSF support is required in all cycles; NCCP permits standard or pegylated G-CSF. Prescribe product, dose and timing individually; the regimen does not supply one universal injection schedule.

Arrange dental/oral assessment, mouth care, dietetic and swallowing support according to need. Review weight, oral intake, pain and hydration throughout chemotherapy and radiotherapy; no automatic feeding-tube decision is generated.

Preserve the CUH high/moderate and docetaxel proforma adjuncts where applicable: omeprazole, local nystatin/chlorhexidine mouth care, breakthrough antiemetics and loperamide. These are historical local reference items requiring current-policy and patient-specific review, not universal prophylaxis or an additional duplicate prescription.

The trial used ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily on Days 5–15; NCCP 00315 permits antimicrobial prophylaxis at the prescribing clinician’s discretion/local policy. It is not a mandatory automatic antibiotic order.

Cisplatin Day 1 carries HIGH emetic risk. Four- or five-day fluorouracil exposure needs a complete prevention/rescue plan through the treatment course; apply NCIS multi-day principles with a reconciled steroid total.
00315.review_status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, oncology-pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

00323.title: Docetaxel 75 / cisplatin 100 / fluorouracil 1,000 · induction before carboplatin chemoradiation
00323.setting: Induction treatment of stage III/IV non-metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, followed by separately prescribed concurrent weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 and radiotherapy if appropriate.
00323.purpose: Treat and shrink the cancer before chemoradiation. The intended benefit belongs to the complete treatment sequence; three induction cycles alone do not complete the plan.
00323.schedule: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² and cisplatin 100 mg/m² on Day 1, with fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day continuously over Days 1–4. Repeat every 21 days for 3 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity develops. If there is no progressive disease and marrow function is adequate, the source describes weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 with radiotherapy for 7 weeks, followed by consideration of surgery. NCCP 00323 says start 3–8 weeks (Days 22–56) after the START of induction cycle 3. Its carboplatin cross-reference says 00322, whereas the matching current regimen is 00332. The 00332 indication text says after COMPLETION of induction, while its treatment paragraph says after START of cycle 3. Resolve the date origin and correct route with the treating team before setting patient dates.

Nausea/vomiting, diarrhoea, mouth inflammation, dehydration and nutritional or swallowing difficulty

The result does not establish that induction is needed for every patient or isolate the contribution of weekly carboplatin.

00324.title: Docetaxel 75 / cisplatin 75 / fluorouracil 750 · induction before radiotherapy
00324.setting: Induction followed by radiotherapy for stage III/IV non-metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; unresectability is determined by the multidisciplinary team.
00324.purpose: Treat and shrink the cancer before radiotherapy. This pathway contains four induction cycles and then separately planned radiotherapy; concurrent carboplatin must not be imported from 00323.
00324.schedule: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² on Day 1, with fluorouracil 750 mg/m²/day on Days 1–5. Repeat every 21 days for 4 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity develops. If there is no progressive disease and marrow function is adequate, radiotherapy starts within 4–7 weeks after completing chemotherapy; surgery is considered afterwards. This source describes radiotherapy, not routine concurrent carboplatin.

00332.title: Carboplatin AUC 1.5 · weekly chemoradiation after induction
00332.setting: Concurrent carboplatin and radiotherapy after induction for stage III/IV non-metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, subject to response and recovery.
00332.purpose: Give carboplatin during radiotherapy as part of the planned combined treatment after induction. Carboplatin is a radiation partner in this phase; it is not a continuation of the TPF medicines.
00332.schedule: Carboplatin AUC 1.5 IV every 7 days for 7 cycles, only while radiotherapy is being delivered. Discontinue carboplatin if radiotherapy is truncated. The treatment paragraph describes a start 3–8 weeks (Days 22–56) after the START of cycle 3 of induction; the indication paragraph says 3–8 weeks after COMPLETION of induction. The MDT must resolve the reference point and set the actual radiotherapy and chemotherapy dates. Confirm the induction route and adequate recovery.
material_risks: Low blood counts with infection, febrile neutropenia, anaemia or bleeding
Platinum hypersensitivity, including serious reactions after prior exposure
Nausea/vomiting, fatigue, kidney/electrolyte effects and possible hearing or nerve injury
Radiotherapy-related mouth/throat pain, swallowing difficulty, skin reaction, nutritional decline and dehydration, discussed with the radiotherapy team
Potential reproductive/fertility effects and treatment-related serious harm
00332.discussion: Discuss the intended benefit and evidence limitations, alternatives, treatment burden, potentially serious or persistent harms, fertility and reproductive precautions, personal priorities and urgent contacts. Use teach-back and the approved local consent process. Confirm the exact indication and current licensed/off-label position.
limitations: Do not present TAX 324 survival differences as the effect of this single concurrent carboplatin phase.
There is an unresolved source discrepancy about the start-date reference point; the patient calendar must be confirmed by the team.
support: NCCP gives no routine G-CSF or additional supportive-care prescription for this weekly phase. Do not carry over induction G-CSF, docetaxel premedication or cisplatin hydration automatically.
Both current weekly carboplatin sources classify emetic risk as MODERATE. Do not infer low risk from the weekly AUC. No routine hypersensitivity premedication is specified.

Arrange dental/oral assessment, mouth care, dietetic and swallowing support according to need. Review weight, oral intake, pain and hydration throughout chemotherapy and radiotherapy; no automatic feeding-tube decision is generated.

These are historical local reference items requiring current-policy and patient-specific review, not universal prophylaxis or an additional duplicate prescription.

00419/head_neck.title: Carboplatin AUC 2 · weekly head and neck chemoradiation
00419/head_neck.setting: NCCP 00419a: stage III/IV locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is contraindicated or not tolerated. This authored content is restricted to the head_neck context; cervical content remains separate.
00419/head_neck.purpose: Use carboplatin with radiotherapy when the team judges cisplatin unsuitable or not tolerated. The intended benefit and uncertainty must be discussed in the context of the patient’s disease, fitness and radiotherapy plan.
00419/head_neck.schedule: Carboplatin AUC 2 IV every 7 days for 6 cycles with radiotherapy. This is the current NCCP 00419 v6 head and neck schedule; do not substitute the AUC 1.5 seven-cycle post-induction pathway. Coordinate each weekly treatment with the radiotherapy and recovery plan. No automatic induction, adjuvant fluorouracil or maintenance phase is added by this regimen.

Platinum hypersensitivity, including serious reactions after prior exposure
Nausea/vomiting, fatigue, kidney/electrolyte effects and possible hearing or nerve injury

limitations: Nasopharyngeal trial results must not be generalised to all head and neck sites or treated as proof of the exact current AUC 2 schedule.
